decisions_requested.title: WoodSpring Airport South — the census bound the wrong candidate, and the fix moves the row into an unassigned ZIP
what_the_owned_evidence_shows: The ORIGINAL candidate ledger (indianapolis_in_candidate_ledger_002.json) holds TWO candidates under the identical name 'WoodSpring Suites Indianapolis Airport South'.

Candidate dc_a11eec6d593c13fe — 4545 Kentucky Avenue, 46221, from OPENSTREETMAP — was REJECTED with disposition OUT_OF_MARKET_BOUNDARY_DECISION and the reason: postal code 46221 is inside the discovery bounding box and is claimed by no corridor in the market registry.
Candidate prior-census::woodspring suites indianapolis airport south — 4402 West Morris Street, 46241, from PRIOR_CENSUS — was ADMITTED_TO_CENSUS and assigned the airport corridor.
So the factory saw the real property, discarded it on a GEOGRAPHY rule, and kept the prior-census copy whose street no source has ever confirmed.
The owned Places lookup for the admitted row (4402 West Morris Street) returned UNBOUND_NO_SANCTIONED_KEY — nothing was findable there under that name.
WoodSpring's own Indiana directory lists exactly THREE Indianapolis properties: Castleton, Airport South and Zionsville. Its Airport South page names 4545 Kentucky Ave, 46221, telephone 3178569533.
decisions_requested.why_this_is_not_a_typo: The street AND the ZIP differ, and they differ because two DIFFERENT candidate records were in play — not because one address was mistyped. Calling it a typo would hide that the market's own geography rule is what discarded the correct record.

supersession_versus_relocation.why: Owned and free evidence cannot show whether a WoodSpring ever operated at 4402 West Morris Street. So I cannot tell you whether this is one building whose address was recorded wrongly (SUPERSESSION) or a business that moved buildings (RELOCATION).
supersession_versus_relocation.does_it_change_the_action: No. Either way the current property is 4545 Kentucky Ave, 46221. The distinction matters for the lineage note, not for the remedy, and I have left it explicitly undetermined rather than guessing.

decisions_requested.the_actual_question: ZIP 46221 is claimed by no Indianapolis corridor, so correcting this address moves the row out of its corridor and re-admits a candidate the market registry already excluded. That is a geography decision, and it is yours.

evidence: 4545 Kentucky Ave is south-west Indianapolis on the Kentucky Avenue diagonal running toward the airport; the airport corridor is 46241 and 46221 adjoins it.
The market boundary note enumerates its exclusions by name and 46221 is NOT among them.

The 'no corridor therefore out of market' rule has ALREADY been overridden by explicit assignment three times: 46202 and 46222 rows sit in the census today by explicit_hotel_ids, and you authorised the same mechanism for 46239 in Order 005.

Eight candidates were rejected on this rule market-wide; 46221 holds two of them — this WoodSpring and a Country Inn & Suites. A blanket ZIP rule would sweep in the Country Inn as well; an explicit assignment admits only the WoodSpring.

options.action: supersede the address to 4545 Kentucky Ave 46221 AND assign this one identity explicitly to indianapolis-in__airport
options.admits: exactly this identity; the Country Inn & Suites in 46221 stays out and returns to you separately
options.consistency: identical to the mechanism you approved in Order 005

options.admits: this WoodSpring AND the Country Inn & Suites AND every future 46221 hotel, automatically

options.option: 3. LEAVE THE ROW AS IT IS
options.consequence: the census keeps an address no source can confirm, and any future route bound to it risks capturing policy for the wrong building — the exact failure this order exists to prevent

options.action: remove the identity from the shadow census
options.consequence: loses a real hotel that demonstrably exists

decisions_requested.recommendation: Option 1. It corrects a binding that is provably wrong, uses the mechanism you have already sanctioned twice, and admits exactly one identity rather than settling 46221 for every future hotel.
decisions_requested.census_impact: count UNCHANGED — a supersession corrects a row in place.
decisions_requested.route_impact: +1 route at $0 once applied; the row currently cannot be routed at all without risking the wrong building.
decisions_requested.publication_impact: NONE today. WoodSpring pages do carry complete first-party pet policy for free, so this row would likely become publishable cheaply afterwards — but that is a later order.

address_diagnostic.method: zero new fetches — the acquisition runs already record every street disagreement they hit, verbatim, so an owned artifact carries a first-party street for each row
address_diagnostic.important_caveat: A recorded street disagreement does NOT prove the census is wrong. It can equally mean the acquisition reached the WRONG PAGE and the refusal was correct. WoodSpring Castleton was provable only because independent evidence — a matching telephone and a single-property brand inventory — showed the PAGE was the right hotel. The other six have no such corroboration yet and must NOT be corrected in bulk.
address_diagnostic.recommended: a future narrow order that corroborates each of the six individually. NOT a 257-row cleanup, and NOT started from the 23%-vs-39% correlation.
